sanskrit: makarākṣaṃ hataṃ śrutvā rāvaṇaḥ samitiṃjayaḥ ādideśātha saṃkruddho raṇāyendrajitaṃ sutam
english: Hearing that Makarākṣa had been slain, Rāvaṇa the conqueror in battle then commanded in fury his son Indrajit to go to the fight.

sanskrit: jahi vīra mahāvīryau bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau adṛśyo dṛśyamāno vā sarvathā tvaṃ balādhikaḥ
english: "Slay, O hero of mighty valour, those two brothers Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa — whether invisible or visible, you in every way surpass them in strength."

sanskrit: tvam apratimakarmāṇam indraṃ jayasi saṃyuge kiṃ punar mānuṣau dṛṣṭvā na vadhiṣyasi saṃyuge
english: "You have defeated Indra himself of unequalled deeds in battle — how then, having seen these mere mortals, will you not slay them in combat?"

sanskrit: tathokto rākṣasendreṇa pratigṛhya pitur vacaḥ yajñabhūmau sa vidhivat pāvakaṃ juhuve ndrajit
english: Thus addressed by the lord of rākṣasas, Indrajit accepted his father's words and duly poured oblations into the sacred fire upon the sacrificial ground.

sanskrit: juhvataś cāpi tatrāgniṃ raktoṣṇīṣadharāḥ striyaḥ ājagmus tatra saṃbhrāntā rākṣasyo yatra rāvaṇiḥ
english: As he offered oblations into the fire there, rākṣasī women wearing red turbans came rushing in agitation to where Rāvaṇa's son stood.

sanskrit: śastrāṇi śarapatrāṇi samidho 'tha vibhītakāḥ lohitāni ca vāsāṃsi sruvaṃ kārṣṇāyasaṃ tathā
english: Weapons, arrows as sacrificial leaves, vibhītaka wood as kindling, red garments, and a ladle of black iron were brought.

sanskrit: sarvato 'gniṃ samāstīrya śarapatraiḥ samantataḥ chāgasya sarvakṛṣṇasya galaṃ jagrāha jīvataḥ
english: Having spread the fire on all sides with arrow-shafts as strewing material, he seized by the throat a living all-black goat.

sanskrit: caruhomasamiddhasya vidhūmasya mahārciṣaḥ babhūvus tāni liṅgāni vijayaṃ darśayanti ca
english: Of the fire blazing for the oblation-offering, smokeless and of great flames, those signs appeared that presaged victory.

sanskrit: pradakṣiṇāvartaśikhas taptahāṭakasaṃnibhaḥ havis tat pratijagrāha pāvakaḥ svayam utthitaḥ
english: With its crest curling clockwise, resembling heated gold, the fire rose up of its own accord and received that oblation.

sanskrit: hutvāgniṃ tarpayitvātha devadānavarākṣasān āruroha rathaśreṣṭham antardhānagataṃ śubham
english: Having offered oblations into the fire and propitiated the gods, dānavas, and rākṣasas, he mounted the finest chariot that had the power of invisibility — that auspicious vehicle.

sanskrit: sa vājibhiś caturbhis tu bāṇaiś ca niśitair yutaḥ āropitamahācāpaḥ śuśubhe syandanottame
english: Drawn by four horses, furnished with sharp arrows, and with his great bow strung and raised, he shone magnificently upon that supreme chariot.

sanskrit: jājvalyamāno vapuṣā tapanīyaparicchadaḥ śaraiś candrārdhacandraiś ca sa rathaḥ samalaṃkṛtaḥ
english: Blazing with bodily splendour, accoutred in gold ornaments, that chariot was fully adorned with arrows — both full-moon-crested and half-moon-headed shafts.

sanskrit: jāmbūnadamahākambur dīptapāvakasaṃnibhaḥ babhūvendrajitaḥ ketur vaidūryasamalaṃkṛtaḥ
english: Indrajit's battle-standard, a great conch-shaped emblem of Jāmbūnada gold, resembling a blazing fire and adorned with vaidūrya gems, blazed forth.

sanskrit: tena cādityakalpena brahmāstreṇa ca pālitaḥ sa babhūva durādharṣo rāvaṇiḥ sumahābalaḥ
english: Protected by that brahma-weapon equal in splendour to the sun, Rāvaṇa's son of tremendous might became invincible.

sanskrit: so 'bhiniryāya nagarād indrajit samitiṃjayaḥ hutvāgniṃ rākṣasair mantrair antardhānagato 'bravīt
english: Indrajit, ever triumphant in battle, sallied forth from the city, offered oblations with rākṣasa mantras, rendered himself invisible, and declared:

sanskrit: adya hatvāhave yau tau mithyā pravrajitau vane jayaṃ pitre pradāsyāmi rāvaṇāya raṇādhikam
english: "Today, by slaying in battle those two who roam the forest under a false pretence of renunciation, I shall bestow victory — an exceeding triumph in war — upon my father Rāvaṇa."

sanskrit: kṛtvā nirvānarām urvīṃ hatvā rāmaṃ salakṣmaṇam kariṣye paramāṃ prītim ity uktvāntaradhīyata
english: "Having made the earth free of Rāma by slaying Rāma together with Lakṣmaṇa, I shall bring my father the highest delight" — saying this, he vanished.

sanskrit: āpapātātha saṃkruddho daśagrīveṇa coditaḥ tīkṣṇakārmukanārācais tīkṣṇas tv indraripū raṇe
english: Then, urged on by the ten-necked one, the keen enemy of Indra fell upon them in fury, fierce in battle with his sharp bow and iron-shafted arrows.

sanskrit: sa dadarśa mahāvīryau nāgau triśirasāv iva sṛjantāv iṣujālāni vīrau vānaramadhyagau
english: He beheld those two heroes of mighty valour standing amid the monkey host, pouring forth networks of arrows like two three-headed serpents.

sanskrit: imau tāv iti saṃcintya sajyaṃ kṛtvā ca kārmukam saṃtatāneṣudhārābhiḥ parjanya iva vṛṣṭimān
english: Recognising them as "these are those two," he strung his bow and poured down unceasing streams of arrows like a rain-cloud pouring rain.

sanskrit: sa tu vaihāyasaṃ prāpya saratho rāmalakṣmaṇau acakṣur viṣaye tiṣṭhan vivyādha niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Taking to the sky with his chariot, he stood beyond the range of their sight and pierced Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa with sharp arrows.

sanskrit: tau tasya śaravegena parītau rāmalakṣmaṇau dhanuṣī saśare kṛtvā divyam astraṃ pracakratuḥ
english: Assailed by the force of his arrows, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa took up their bows with arrows nocked and discharged divine weapons.

sanskrit: pracchādayantau gaganaṃ śarajālair mahābalau tam astraiḥ surasaṃkāśau naiva pasparśatuḥ śaraiḥ
english: Though the two mighty ones, resplendent as gods, covered the sky with nets of arrows, they could not touch him with their shafts or weapons.

sanskrit: sa hi dhūmāndhakāraṃ ca cakre pracchādayan nabhaḥ diśaś cāntardadhe śrīmān nīhāratamasāvṛtaḥ
english: For that glorious one created a darkness of smoke, veiling the sky, and the directions vanished, enveloped in misty gloom.

sanskrit: naiva jyātalanirghoṣo na ca nemikhurasvanaḥ śuśruve caratas tasya na ca rūpaṃ prakāśate
english: Neither the twang of his bowstring, nor the sound of his chariot's wheel-rims and hoofbeats could be heard as he moved; nor did his form become visible.

sanskrit: ghanāndhakāre timire śaravarṣam ivādbhutam sa vavarṣa mahābāhur nārācaśaravṛṣṭibhiḥ
english: In the dense dark gloom, the long-armed one rained down what seemed a wondrous shower of arrows — a downpour of iron-shafted shafts.

sanskrit: sa rāmaṃ sūryasaṃkāśaiḥ śarair dattavaro bhṛśam vivyādha samare kruddhaḥ sarvagātreṣu rāvaṇiḥ
english: Rāvaṇa's son, empowered by a boon, wounded Rāma grievously with arrows bright as the sun, striking every limb in fury during battle.

sanskrit: tau hanyamānau nārācair dhārābhir iva parvatau hemapuṅkhān naravyāghrau tigmān mumucatuḥ śarān
english: Struck by the iron-shafted arrows as if by torrents, those two tiger-men, though like mountains under assault, released sharp arrows with golden feathering.

sanskrit: antarikṣaṃ samāsādya rāvaṇiṃ kaṅkapatriṇaḥ nikṛtya patagā bhūmau petus te śoṇitokṣitāḥ
english: Reaching into the sky to reach Rāvaṇa's son, those heron-feathered arrows were cut apart and fell to the earth soaked in blood.

sanskrit: atimātraṃ śaraugheṇa pīḍyamānau narottamau tān iṣūn patato bhallair anekair nicakartatuḥ
english: Those two foremost of men, excessively tormented by the flood of arrows, cut apart those falling shafts with many broad-headed arrows.

sanskrit: yato hi dadṛśāte tau śarān nipatitāñ śitān tatas tato dāśarathī sasṛjāte 'stram uttamam
english: Wherever those two sons of Daśaratha saw sharp arrows descending, there and thence they released supreme weapons.

sanskrit: rāvaṇis tu diśaḥ sarvā rathenātirathaḥ patan vivyādha tau dāśarathī laghv astro niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: But Rāvaṇa's son, a supreme chariot-warrior, roaming all directions with his chariot and swift in his weapons, pierced those two sons of Daśaratha with sharp arrows.

sanskrit: tenātividdhau tau vīrau rukmapuṅkhaiḥ susaṃhataiḥ babhūvatur dāśarathī puṣpitāv iva kiṃśukau
english: Those two heroes, the sons of Daśaratha, pierced excessively by him with well-compacted gold-feathered shafts, looked like two flowering kiṃśuka trees.

sanskrit: nāsya veda gatiṃ kaś cin na ca rūpaṃ dhanuḥ śarān na cānyad viditaṃ kiṃ cit sūryasyevābhrasaṃplave
english: No one could discern his movements, nor his form, bow, or arrows — nothing else whatsoever could be perceived, as when the sun is engulfed by clouds.

sanskrit: tena viddhāś ca harayo nihatāś ca gatāsavaḥ babhūvuḥ śataśas tatra patitā dharaṇītale
english: Pierced by him, monkeys slain and bereft of life lay fallen there on the surface of the earth by the hundreds.

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇas tu susaṃkruddho bhrātaraṃ vākyam abravīt brāhmam astraṃ prayokṣyāmi vadhārthaṃ sarvarakṣasām
english: Lakṣmaṇa, greatly enraged, spoke to his brother: "I shall deploy the brāhma-weapon for the purpose of slaying all rākṣasas."

sanskrit: tam uvāca tato rāmo lakṣmaṇaṃ śubhalakṣaṇam naikasya heto rakṣāṃsi pṛthivyāṃ hantum arhasi
english: Then Rāma spoke to Lakṣmaṇa of auspicious marks: "For the sake of one alone you should not slay all rākṣasas on the earth."

sanskrit: ayudhyamānaṃ pracchannaṃ prāñjaliṃ śaraṇāgatam palāyantaṃ pramattaṃ vā na tvaṃ hantum ihārhasi
english: "One who is not fighting, one concealed, one with palms joined, one who has sought refuge, one who is fleeing, or one who is heedless — you should not slay any such here."

sanskrit: asyaiva tu vadhe yatnaṃ kariṣyāvo mahābala ādekṣyāvo mahāvegān astrān āśīviṣopamān
english: "Let us make the effort for the slaying of this one alone, O mighty one — let us release swift weapons terrible as venomous serpents."

sanskrit: tam enaṃ māyinaṃ kṣudram antarhitarathaṃ balāt rākṣasaṃ nihaniṣyanti dṛṣṭvā vānarayūthapāḥ
english: "This petty rākṣasa who wields illusion, his chariot hidden by force — the monkey troop-leaders will slay him once they spot him."

sanskrit: yady eṣa bhūmiṃ viśate divaṃ vā rasātalaṃ vāpi nabhastalaṃ vā evaṃ nigūḍho 'pi mamāstradagdhaḥ patiṣyate bhūmitale gatāsuḥ
english: "Even if this one should enter the earth, or the sky, or the netherworld, or the vault of heaven — even thus concealed, he shall be scorched by my weapon and fall lifeless to the ground."

sanskrit: ity evam uktvā vacanaṃ mahātmā raghupravīraḥ plavagarṣabhair vṛtaḥ vadhāya raudrasya nṛśaṃsakarmaṇas tadā mahātmā tvaritaṃ nirīkṣate
english: Having spoken thus, the great-souled foremost hero of the Raghus, surrounded by the best of the monkeys, then eagerly watched — the great-souled one — for the slaying of that ferocious and cruel-deeded one.

sanskrit: vijñāya tu manas tasya rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ saṃnivṛtyāhavāt tasmāt praviveśa puraṃ tataḥ
english: Perceiving the resolve of the great-souled Rāghava, Indrajit withdrew from that battle and re-entered the city.

sanskrit: so 'nusmṛtya vadhaṃ teṣāṃ rākṣasānāṃ tarasvinām krodhatāmrekṣaṇaḥ śūro nirjagāma mahādyutiḥ
english: That hero of great splendour, recalling the slaughter of those swift rākṣasas, went forth again with eyes reddened by anger.

sanskrit: sa paścimena dvāreṇa niryayau rākṣasair vṛtaḥ indrajit tu mahāvīryaḥ paulastyo devakaṇṭakaḥ
english: Indrajit, of mighty valour, descendant of Pulastya, the scourge of the gods, went out through the western gate surrounded by rākṣasas.

sanskrit: indrajit tu tato dṛṣṭvā bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau raṇāyābhyudyatau vīrau māyāṃ prāduṣkarot tadā
english: Indrajit, seeing those two warrior brothers Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa arrayed for battle, then conjured up an illusion.

sanskrit: indrajit tu rathe sthāpya sītāṃ māyāmayīṃ tadā balena mahatāvṛtya tasyā vadham arocayat
english: Indrajit placed on his chariot an illusory Sītā wrought of māyā, and surrounded by a great army, resolved upon her slaying.

sanskrit: mohanārthaṃ tu sarveṣāṃ buddhiṃ kṛtvā sudurmatiḥ hantuṃ sītāṃ vyavasito vānarābhimukho yayau
english: That one of utterly evil mind, with the intention of bewildering everyone and resolved to slay Sītā, set out toward the monkeys.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā tv abhiniryāntaṃ nagaryāḥ kānanaukasaḥ utpetur abhisaṃkruddhāḥ śilāhastā yuyutsavaḥ
english: Seeing him sally forth from the city, the forest-dwellers sprang up, furious and eager for battle, rocks in their hands.

sanskrit: hanūmān puratas teṣāṃ jagāma kapikuñjaraḥ pragṛhya sumahac chṛṅgaṃ parvatasya durāsadam
english: Hanūmān, that bull among monkeys, went in front of them all, grasping a mighty mountain peak that was difficult to assail.

sanskrit: sa dadarśa hatānandāṃ sītām indrajito rathe ekaveṇīdharāṃ dīnām upavāsakṛśānanām
english: He saw Sītā — stripped of joy — on Indrajit's chariot: her hair in a single braid, miserable, her face gaunt from fasting.

sanskrit: parikliṣṭaikavasanām amṛjāṃ rāghavapriyām rajomalābhyām āliptaiḥ sarvagātrair varastriyam
english: Clad in a single worn garment, unwashed, every limb smeared with dust and grime — that beloved of Rāghava, that most beautiful of women.

sanskrit: tāṃ nirīkṣya muhūrtaṃ tu maithilīm adhyavasya ca bāṣpaparyākulamukho hanūmān vyathito 'bhavat
english: Having gazed upon the Maithilī for a moment and having made a firm judgment, Hanūmān became distressed, his face overwhelmed with tears.

sanskrit: abravīt tāṃ tu śokārtāṃ nirānandāṃ tapasvinām dṛṣṭvā rathe stitāṃ sītāṃ rākṣasendrasutāśritām
english: He saw her — grief-stricken, joyless, wretched Sītā seated on the chariot under the sway of the son of the lord of rākṣasas — and spoke.

sanskrit: kiṃ samarthitam asyeti cintayan sa mahākapiḥ saha tair vānaraśreṣṭhair abhyadhāvata rāvaṇim
english: That great monkey, thinking "What does this one intend?", together with those foremost of monkeys charged toward the son of Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: tad vānarabalaṃ dṛṣṭvā rāvaṇiḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ kṛtvā viśokaṃ nistriṃśaṃ mūrdhni sītāṃ parāmṛśat
english: Seeing that monkey force, the son of Rāvaṇa, overcome with rage, drew his gleaming sword and grasped Sītā by the hair.

sanskrit: taṃ striyaṃ paśyatāṃ teṣāṃ tāḍayām āsa rāvaṇiḥ krośantīṃ rāma rāmeti māyayā yojitāṃ rathe
english: As they all watched, the son of Rāvaṇa struck that woman — the one joined to the chariot by illusion — who cried out "Rāma! Rāma!"

sanskrit: gṛhītamūrdhajāṃ dṛṣṭvā hanūmān dainyam āgataḥ duḥkhajaṃ vārinetrābhyām utsṛjan mārutātmajaḥ abravīt paruṣaṃ vākyaṃ krodhād rakṣo'dhipātmajam
english: Seeing her seized by the hair, the son of the Wind, Hanūmān, overcome by anguish and shedding tears born of grief from both eyes, spoke harsh words in fury to the son of the lord of rākṣasas:

sanskrit: durātmann ātmanāśāya keśapakṣe parāmṛśaḥ brahmarṣīṇāṃ kule jāto rākṣasīṃ yonim āśritaḥ dhik tvāṃ pāpasamācāraṃ yasya te matir īdṛśī
english: "Evil-minded one, you seize a woman by her hair to bring about your own destruction! Born in the lineage of brahmarṣis yet fallen into the rākṣasa species — shame on you of sinful conduct, whose mind is of such a kind!"

sanskrit: nṛśaṃsānārya durvṛtta kṣudra pāpaparākrama anāryasyedṛśaṃ karma ghṛṇā te nāsti nirghṛṇa
english: "Cruel one, ignoble one, of evil conduct, petty one, whose valour is that of a sinner — such a deed is fit only for the base; you have no compassion, O merciless one!"

sanskrit: cyutā gṛhāc ca rājyāc ca rāmahastāc ca maithilī kiṃ tavaiṣāparāddhā hi yad enāṃ hantum icchasi
english: "The Maithilī, fallen from her home, from her kingdom, from Rāma's side — what wrong has she done you that you wish to slay her?"

sanskrit: sītāṃ ca hatvā na ciraṃ jīviṣyasi kathaṃ cana vadhārhakarmaṇānena mama hastagato hy asi
english: "Having slain Sītā, you shall not live long by any means — by this deed worthy of death you have indeed come into my hands."

sanskrit: ye ca strīghātināṃ lokā lokavadhyaiś ca kutsitāḥ iha jīvitam utsṛjya pretya tān pratilapsyase
english: "And the worlds that await slayers of women — those loathsome worlds condemned by all — those shall you attain, having relinquished life here and gone to the hereafter."

sanskrit: iti bruvāṇo hanumān sāyudhair haribhir vṛtaḥ abhyadhāvata saṃkruddho rākṣasendrasutaṃ prati
english: Saying this, Hanūmān, surrounded by armed monkeys, charged in great fury toward the son of the lord of rākṣasas.

sanskrit: āpatantaṃ mahāvīryaṃ tad anīkaṃ vanaukasām rakṣasāṃ bhīmavegānām anīkena nyavārayat
english: That host of terrible-swift rākṣasas checked the charging army of forest-dwellers, that host of mighty valour.

sanskrit: sa tāṃ bāṇasahasreṇa vikṣobhya harivāhinīm hariśreṣṭhaṃ hanūmantam indrajit pratyuvāca ha
english: Having troubled the monkey-army with a thousand arrows, Indrajit then addressed Hanūmān, that foremost of monkeys:

sanskrit: sugrīvas tvaṃ ca rāmaś ca yannimittam ihāgatāḥ tāṃ haniṣyāmi vaidehīm adyaiva tava paśyataḥ
english: "The Vaidehī — for whose sake Sugrīva, you yourself, and Rāma have come here — her I shall slay today, even as you watch."

sanskrit: imāṃ hatvā tato rāmaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ tvāṃ ca vānara sugrīvaṃ ca vadhiṣyāmi taṃ cānāryaṃ vibhīṣaṇam
english: "After slaying her, I shall then slay Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa, you, O monkey, Sugrīva, and that ignoble Vibhīṣaṇa."

sanskrit: na hantavyāḥ striyaś ceti yad bravīṣi plavaṃgama pīḍā karam amitrāṇāṃ yat syāt kartavyam eta tat
english: "As for what you say, O leaping one — 'women must not be slain' — whatever would cause pain to one's enemies, that is what must be done."

sanskrit: tam evam uktvā rudatīṃ sītāṃ māyāmayīṃ tataḥ śitadhāreṇa khaḍgena nijaghānendrajit svayam
english: Having spoken thus, Indrajit then personally struck that weeping illusory Sītā with his sharp-edged sword.

sanskrit: yajñopavītamārgeṇa chinnā tena tapasvinī sā pṛthivyāṃ pṛthuśroṇī papāta priyadarśanā
english: Cut by him along the line of the sacred thread, that wretched woman of broad hips, fair to behold, fell to the earth.

sanskrit: tām indrajitstriyaṃ hatvā hanūmantam uvāca ha mayā rāmasya paśyemāṃ kopena ca niṣūditām
english: Having slain that woman, Indrajit said to Hanūmān: "Look — she has been struck down by me in anger before your very eyes, this one who was Rāma's."

sanskrit: tataḥ khaḍgena mahatā hatvā tām indrajit svayam hṛṣṭaḥ sa ratham āsthāya vinanāda mahāsvanam
english: Then Indrajit, having slain her personally with his great sword, mounted his chariot in delight and let out a mighty roar.

sanskrit: vānarāḥ śuśruvuḥ śabdam adūre pratyavasthitāḥ vyāditāsyasya nadatas tad durgaṃ saṃśritasya tu
english: The monkeys stationed nearby heard that roar — the roar of one with gaping mouth, who had taken refuge in that stronghold.

sanskrit: tathā tu sītāṃ vinihatya durmatiḥ prahṛṣṭacetāḥ sa babhūva rāvaṇiḥ taṃ hṛṣṭarūpaṃ samudīkṣya vānarā viṣaṇṇarūpāḥ samabhipradudruvuḥ
english: That evil-minded son of Rāvaṇa, having thus slain Sītā, became joyful at heart; seeing him exultant in aspect, the monkeys became crestfallen in appearance and fled in all directions.

sanskrit: śrutvā taṃ bhīmanirhrādaṃ śakrāśanisamasvanam vīkṣamāṇā diśaḥ sarvā dudruvur vānararṣabhāḥ
english: Hearing that terrible roar, equal in sound to Indra's thunderbolt, the bull-like monkeys gazed in all directions and fled.

sanskrit: tān uvāca tataḥ sarvān hanūmān mārutātmajaḥ viṣaṇṇavadanān dīnāṃs trastān vidravataḥ pṛthak
english: Then Hanūmān, son of the Wind, spoke to all of them — their faces downcast, miserable, frightened, scattering in different directions:

sanskrit: kasmād viṣaṇṇavadanā vidravadhvaṃ plavaṃgamāḥ tyaktayuddhasamutsāhāḥ śūratvaṃ kva nu vo gatam
english: "Why do you flee with downcast faces, O leaping monkeys, your ardour for battle abandoned? Where has your heroism gone?"

sanskrit: pṛṣṭhato 'nuvrajadhvaṃ mām agrato yāntam āhave śūrair abhijanopetair ayuktaṃ hi nivartitum
english: "Follow behind me as I go forward in battle — it is not fitting for those of heroic lineage to turn back."

sanskrit: evam uktāḥ susaṃkruddhā vāyuputreṇa dhīmatā śailaśṛṅgān drumāṃś caiva jagṛhur hṛṣṭamānasāḥ
english: Thus addressed by the wise son of the Wind, greatly enraged and with gladdened hearts, they seized mountain peaks and trees.

sanskrit: abhipetuś ca garjanto rākṣasān vānararṣabhāḥ parivārya hanūmantam anvayuś ca mahāhave
english: Those bull-like monkeys charged at the rākṣasas roaring, and surrounding Hanūmān they followed him in the great battle.

sanskrit: sa tair vānaramukhyais tu hanūmān sarvato vṛtaḥ hutāśana ivārciṣmān adahac chatruvāhinīm
english: Hanūmān, encircled on all sides by those foremost monkeys, blazed like a fire with flames and burned the enemy's army.

sanskrit: sa rākṣasānāṃ kadanaṃ cakāra sumahākapiḥ vṛto vānarasainyena kālāntakayamopamaḥ
english: That mighty great monkey, surrounded by the monkey army and resembling Yama the lord of death at the end of an age, wrought slaughter among the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: sa tu śokena cāviṣṭaḥ krodhena ca mahākapiḥ hanūmān rāvaṇi rathe mahatīṃ pātayac chilām
english: That great monkey Hanūmān, seized by grief and rage alike, hurled a great boulder at the chariot of the son of Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: tām āpatantīṃ dṛṣṭvaiva rathaḥ sārathinā tadā vidheyāśva samāyuktaḥ sudūram apavāhitaḥ
english: Seeing it hurtling down, the chariot — fitted with well-trained horses and its charioteer — was at once driven far away.

sanskrit: tam indrajitam aprāpya rathathaṃ sahasārathim viveśa dharaṇīṃ bhittvā sā śilāvyartham udyatā
english: Not reaching Indrajit along with his chariot and charioteer, that boulder — raised in vain — split the earth and entered the ground.

sanskrit: patitāyāṃ śilāyāṃ tu rakṣasāṃ vyathitā camūḥ tam abhyadhāvañ śataśo nadantaḥ kānanaukasaḥ
english: When the boulder fell, the rākṣasa army was shaken; the forest-dwellers charged at them by the hundreds, roaring.

sanskrit: te drumāṃś ca mahākāyā giriśṛṅgāṇi codyatāḥ cikṣipur dviṣatāṃ madhye vānarā bhīmavikramāḥ
english: Those monkeys of massive bodies and terrible prowess, aroused, hurled trees and mountain peaks into the midst of the enemy.

sanskrit: vānarair tair mahāvīryair ghorarūpā niśācarāḥ vīryād abhihatā vṛkṣair vyaveṣṭanta raṇakṣitau
english: Those night-wanderers of dreadful form, struck with force by those mighty-valorous monkeys with their trees, writhed on the battle-ground.

sanskrit: svasainyam abhivīkṣyātha vānarārditam indrajit pragṛhītāyudhaḥ kruddhaḥ parān abhimukho yayau
english: Seeing his own army tormented by the monkeys, Indrajit took up his weapons and in fury turned to face the enemy.

sanskrit: sa śaraughān avasṛjan svasainyenābhisaṃvṛtaḥ jaghāna kapiśārdūlān subahūn dṛṣṭavikramaḥ
english: Releasing torrents of arrows, surrounded by his own army and displaying his valour, he slew very many of those tiger-monkeys.

sanskrit: śūlair aśanibhiḥ khaḍgaiḥ paṭṭasaiḥ kūṭamudgaraiḥ te cāpy anucarāṃs tasya vānarā jaghnur āhave
english: The monkeys in turn slew his attendants in battle with spears, thunderbolt-weapons, swords, broad blades, and blunt iron clubs.

sanskrit: saskandhaviṭapaiḥ sālaiḥ śilābhiś ca mahābalaiḥ hanūmān kadanaṃ cakre rakṣasāṃ bhīmakarmaṇām
english: With śāla trees bearing their branches and boughs, and with boulders, the mighty Hanūmān wrought carnage among those rākṣasas of terrible deeds.

sanskrit: sa nivārya parānīkam abravīt tān vanaukasaḥ hanūmān saṃnivartadhvaṃ na naḥ sādhyam idaṃ balam
english: Checking the enemy's army, Hanūmān spoke to those forest-dwellers: "Turn back — this force cannot be overcome by us."

sanskrit: tyaktvā prāṇān viceṣṭanto rāma priyacikīrṣavaḥ yannimittaṃ hi yudhyāmo hatā sā janakātmajā
english: "We who fight abandoning our lives, wishing to do what is dear to Rāma — the daughter of Janaka for whose sake we fight has been slain."

sanskrit: imam arthaṃ hi vijñāpya rāmaṃ sugrīvam eva ca tau yat pratividhāsyete tat kariṣyāmahe vayam
english: "Having reported this matter to Rāma and to Sugrīva, we shall do whatever those two shall determine in response."

sanskrit: ity uktvā vānaraśreṣṭho vārayan sarvavānarān śanaiḥ śanair asaṃtrastaḥ sabalaḥ sa nyavartata
english: Having spoken thus, that foremost of monkeys, restraining all the monkeys, withdrew slowly and deliberately, unafraid, with his forces.

sanskrit: sa tu prekṣya hanūmantaṃ vrajantaṃ yatra rāghavaḥ nikumbhilām adhiṣṭhāya pāvakaṃ juhuve ndrajit
english: Seeing Hanūmān departing toward where Rāghava was, Indrajit repaired to Nikumbhilā and poured oblations into the fire.

sanskrit: yajñabhūmyāṃ tu vidhivat pāvakas tena rakṣasā hūyamānaḥ prajajvāla homaśoṇitabhuk tadā
english: Upon the sacrificial ground, the fire blazed up, ritually invoked by that rākṣasa, consuming the oblation of blood.

sanskrit: so 'rciḥ pinaddho dadṛśe homaśoṇitatarpitaḥ saṃdhyāgata ivādityaḥ sa tīvrāgniḥ samutthitaḥ
english: That flame, dense and radiant, was seen — satiated by the blood-oblation — rising up, that fierce fire, like the sun arrived at the twilight.

sanskrit: athendrajid rākṣasabhūtaye tu juhāva havyaṃ vidhinā vidhānavat dṛṣṭvā vyatiṣṭhanta ca rākṣasās te mahāsamūheṣu nayānayajñāḥ
english: Then Indrajit, for the welfare of the rākṣasas, offered the oblation according to rule and ordinance; and seeing this, those rākṣasas took their stations in great multitudes — those who knew the rites of sound and unsound sacrifice.
